text.p: The Castle Cup of Africa, a tournament for teams in the southern African region, has been re-launched with an expanded line-up, officials announced on Wednesday.
The tournament, which ran into trouble with FIFA last year for failing to obtain the necessary sanction, will start on March 1 with four new countries added to its original field of five.

Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi and Swaziland have been added to the entries and the format of the competition changed, said the Confederation of Southern African Football Associations (Cosafa), who have taken over the running of the event.
The other participants are Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
A first round of single knockout matches will be played next month and the four winners will join Tanzania in the final round group phase to determine the tournament winner.
The group matches will be played from April through to July.
Prize money of almost US$250 000 is being offered by the sponsors, South African Breweries.

Tanzania and Zimbabwe were heavily fined by FIFA last October for playing the opening match of the tournament without FIFA sanction. But officials said FIFA had now granted permission for the event to go ahead.
